_how_to: One section per metric. This file is where a metric's name, wording, dictionary card and known limits live.

Known limits: one line each, {"limit": ..., "mitigation": ..., "status": ...}. Status is usually Mitigated, Partly mitigated, Planned or No mitigation yet. Add a line to add a limit; delete the line to remove it.

card = the dictionary card (Risk it watches, population, time basis and so on). wording = the plain-language phrases the pages use. counting = which files the metric needs and how its items are described; the counting itself is the metric's function in backend/trust/measure.py (named under code).

status: Measured (counted and scored), In progress (being built; not scored yet), Planned (designed, no data source yet) or Coming soon (no source agreed). Anything but Measured counts in no score and shows as No data.
After an edit: run the tests (python -m pytest -q tests), deploy, then update the month. Locked months keep their numbers; wording shows as edited.
Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.

checks.name: Main branch protected
checks.rule: Branch protection or an active ruleset covers the default branch. Without it, the other four checks can't pass.

checks.name: Review required
checks.rule: At least one approving review is required before a change is merged.

checks.name: Independent approval
checks.rule: The most recent push must be approved by someone other than the person who pushed it.

checks.name: History can't be rewritten
checks.rule: Force pushes and deleting the branch are both blocked.

checks.name: No one can skip the rules
checks.rule: Admins are held to the rules and nobody has bypass rights.

card.definition: Count of eligible privileged accounts (per IAM standard) vaulted in CyberArk. Pass/fail: Green when every eligible account is vaulted; Amber when any is not; Red when an account belonging to a Tier 0/1 app is not.

card.pass_fail_rule: Pass/fail: Green when every eligible account is vaulted; Amber when any is not; Red when an account belonging to a Tier 0/1 app is not.
card.risk_monitored: Privileged accounts are misused or compromised without rotation or a record of use.
card.risk: Privileged accounts that are not vaulted may be misused or compromised without credential rotation or a record of who used them. Vaulting does not by itself show that the access was appropriate.

card.exclusions_text: Only those listed in the IAM standard.

TE-01.name: Change ticket adoption
TE-01.definition: Share of a family's deployed production changes that went through TCC.

card.definition: Share of a family's deployed production changes that went through TCC.
card.time_text: Flow during the month: counted in the month the change ticket was created (for TCC, the last deployment date is used only when the created date is blank; for Non-TCC, the last updated date)
card.time_note: A change counts in the month its ticket was created. TE-02 counts releases a little later, in the month their 7-day revert window closes, so in any one month the two metrics can cover different changes. That is expected: each is counted when its answer is known.

open_items.item: Emergency change treatment.
Link this metric to its risk-register entry; confirm the indicator type and the COBIT 2019 mapping.

card.risk_monitored: Production changes skip the change control route.
card.risk: Every production change should go through TCC, the firm's change control route. A change made outside TCC skips its review and approval steps, so unreviewed changes can reach production. This is the core program-change control.
card.population: Production changes deployed in the month, from both the TCC and the Non-TCC exports, counted in the month the ticket was created. A change counts as through TCC when it is in the TCC export, Standard changes included. Non-TCC changes count as deployed when their Status is Completed, Resolved, Monitoring or Client. A change in both exports counts once, as TCC.
card.exclusions_text: Changes with no production deployment recorded (TCC), or with a status that doesn't mean deployed (Non-TCC).
card.zero_text: No deployed changes in the month: not scored.

known_limits.limit: Going through TCC doesn't show that a change was approved before it was deployed.
known_limits.mitigation: None yet in this metric. The TCC file still carries the approval time, so it can be checked again later.

known_limits.limit: The Non-TCC export has no deployment date.
known_limits.mitigation: The month comes from the ticket's Created Date, the same rule as TCC. Working rule until Change Management confirms (Q-NTCC-01).

known_limits.limit: Which Non-TCC statuses mean a change was deployed isn't confirmed yet.
known_limits.mitigation: Working rule: Completed, Resolved, Monitoring and Client count as deployed (Q-NTCC-02).

known_limits.limit: A Non-TCC change with no author email can't be placed with a family.
known_limits.mitigation: It shows as Not yet mapped on the firm page, never hidden.

known_limits.limit: A change could appear in both exports.
known_limits.mitigation: It counts once, as TCC, and is listed when the month is mapped.

known_limits.limit: Many deployments can be linked to one general ticket.
known_limits.mitigation: None yet. There is no check for tickets linked to many deployments.

counting.empty_reason: No deployed changes this month: not scored

code.what: Counts deployed changes through TCC out of all deployed changes per family
Reads the TCC export and flags each change
Reads the Non-TCC export and flags each deployed change

TE-02.name: Release revert rate (7 days)
TE-02.definition: Share of production releases reverted or rolled back within 7 days.

card.definition: Share of production releases backed out within 7 days.
card.time_text: Each release counts in the month its 7-day revert window ends (release date + 7 days)
card.time_note: A release counts in the month its 7-day revert window closes (release date + 7 days): a release on 28 September counts in October. TE-01 counts changes in the month their ticket was created, so in any one month the two metrics can cover different changes. That is expected: each is counted when its answer is known.

open_items.item: Production defect definition and source; whether a hotfix counts as a revert.
Link this metric to its risk-register entry; confirm the indicator type and the COBIT 2019 mapping.

card.risk_monitored: Weak testing lets bad releases reach production.
card.risk: Releases that have to be backed out point to weak pre-production testing, and bad releases that reach production can affect clients.
card.population: Production releases through TCC whose 7-day revert window ended in the month. A release is reverted when its overall outcome is 40, 50, 60 or 90 (backed out, including a backout started by the client).
card.exclusions_text: Outcome 95 (obsoleted). Outcome 99 (unknown) and a blank outcome are left out of the rate and counted separately.
card.zero_text: No releases in the month: not scored.

known_limits.limit: Releases late in a month have not finished their 7-day window.
known_limits.mitigation: Each release counts in the month its window ends (owner, 2 Nov 2026), so none is counted early.

known_limits.limit: A release with an unknown (99) or blank outcome can't be judged.
known_limits.mitigation: Left out of the rate and counted separately. The counts are not shown on the page yet.

known_limits.limit: A low rate can mean good testing, or fixing forward instead of backing out.
known_limits.mitigation: Read together with UN-01 (incidents). There is no count of quick fixes yet.

known_limits.limit: Bundling changes into fewer releases shrinks the count.
known_limits.mitigation: None yet. There is no release-count trend.

counting.empty_reason: No production deployments this month: not scored

code.what: Counts releases and reverts in each 7-day window
